args: Analyze the ownership cycle/re-entrant destruction vulnerability rooted in SkPictureShader::refBitmapShader in skia/src/shaders/SkPictureShader.cpp. What minimally invasive fix should prevent a cached BitmapShaderRec from strongly retaining the source SkPicture through SkPictureImageGenerator, while preserving picture-shader rendering and cache behavior? Check relevant APIs for rasterizing a picture into an image without generator ownership, and mention historical/upstream patterns if known.

The ASan report shows BitmapShaderRec destruction during SkResourceCache::checkMessages/purgeSharedID destroys SkImageShader -> lazy SkImage -> SkPictureImageGenerator -> SkBigPicture -> SkRecord -> recorded SkPaint, which unrefs an already destroyed nested SkPictureShader. The cache entry created by refBitmapShader therefore creates a re-entrant ownership graph. The trigger uses nested recorded pictures and mock GPU draws. I am considering replacing the lazy picture-backed image with an eagerly rasterized image/bitmap, or changing cache ownership, but need to preserve scale, color space, tile modes, and matrix semantics. Relevant source is skia/src/shaders/SkPictureShader.cpp, especially BitmapShaderRec and refBitmapShader.
